exclude.basis: A cluster in both catalogues is drawn once, from Jordán et al.'s Hubble position: 33 of Côté et al.'s clusters lie within 0.8 arcsec of one of theirs and the next nearest pair is 2.6 arcsec apart, so 1.5 arcsec separates the same cluster from a neighbour.

frame.converter: Each sky position at a depth drawn from the spheroid's density along its sight line (frame.spheroid).

spheroid.basis: The spheroid the volume's light is spread through (src/objects/m49-volume/source/experiment.json shapePrior): Kormendy et al.'s (2009) Table 1 major-axis Sérsic fit to NGC 4472 (n = 5.99, half-light radius 269.29 arcsec, 21.8 kpc at 16.7 Mpc), axis along M49's minor axis in the plane of the sky, ending at 3.906 half-light radii, where their Table 3 profile stops. Each cluster's depth is drawn from it, not measured.

meaning: Globular clusters of M49 with a measured radial velocity (Côté et al. 2003, Table 2, class GC) that Jordán et al.'s (2009) Hubble catalogue does not already list: one dot per cluster at its catalogue position.

appearance.note: Presentation only: the Milky Way globular clusters' warm orange.
